clue.text: Condition of Abel's dotage?

parts.note: Abel was the younger son of Adam and Eve in Genesis, so any senility he had would be that of the family's number-two offspring

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for senile decline in old age is read literally: Abel was the second child born to Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for the feeble, childish state of extreme old age.

clue.text: Follow fashion to make current easy progress

definitions.meaning: to go along with what everyone else is doing
literally, to let the flow of the sea carry you along

explanation.surface: Advice to conform, put in terms of being carried along by the flow.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to conform; literally a swimmer moving with the flow of water goes easily.

clue.text: Seek votes from the cloth, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the cloth is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: canvas is a heavy cloth used for sails and tents

explanation.surface: Someone tries to drum up support from the clergy, 'the cloth'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' usually means the clergy; here it is literal fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to go round asking people for their electoral support.

clue.text: Unsophisticated note article provided

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
provided means if, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: A short memo says something naive, on condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A naive person is innocent and lacks worldliness, a synonym of the clue word.

clue.text: Five scores making land mark for batsman

definitions.meaning: a score is twenty, so five of them make a hundred
the milestone of a hundred runs that a cricket batsman hopes to reach

explanation.surface: A cricketer reaches a landmark total.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman's hundred runs in one innings is a celebrated milestone; 'land mark' plays on landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred of anything, years or runs, is the number given by five twenties.

clue.text: Superficially irritated, but very keen

definitions.meaning: having skin that is irritated on its surface
eager, impatient to do something

explanation.surface: Someone with skin trouble who is also eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the skin prickles; figuratively one is impatient and eager to act.

clue.text: Solution slowly taken in, if you're patient?

definitions.text: Solution slowly taken in, if you're patient?

parts.words: Solution slowly taken in, if you're patient?
parts.note: patient means a hospital patient, not someone who waits calmly, receiving a liquid by slow intravenous feed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' reads as an adjective about waiting, but it is the hospital noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital device feeds liquid medication into a vein slowly, a bit at a time.

clue.text: Policeman to find if force is corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Investigating whether the police force is crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is corrupt' rearranges IF and FORCE together.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer is a constable or other member of the police.

clue.text: Follow custom-no tip ping on board

definitions.meaning: keep to the usual way and cause no disturbance
literally, do not tilt the vessel you are on

explanation.surface: Instructions to conform and not to leave gratuities on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipping' suggests gratuities; here it is tilting a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a warning against upsetting the status quo; literally it warns against tilting a vessel.

clue.text: One has a local name for wicked sinning

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted or perverse, prompting a rearrangement of the next word

explanation.surface: A pub name is chosen for being wicked, about sinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for a neighbourhood pub; the board outside showing its name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The board hanging outside a pub displays the name of the British 'local'.

clue.text: Back off being in feature, it's thin material

indicators.note: being in shows one piece placed inside the facial feature

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face

indicators.note: back signals that the word off is written in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone retreats inside, describing a flimsy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back off' reads as a phrase meaning retreat; split it so 'Back' is the reversal signal and 'off' its fodder, set inside the facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a light, sheer fabric of silk or nylon.

clue.text: From which Britons used to die, we hear, in battle

definitions.text: From which Britons used to die

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds the same in non-rhotic British speech

parts.note: fought in a war, warred

explanation.surface: Ancient Britons dying in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Die' is a pun on dye: ancient Britons coloured themselves with the plant's blue extract. In British speech the r of WARRED is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant yields a blue colouring used by ancient Britons to stain their bodies.

clue.text: Bird is to cower

definitions.meaning: a small game bird of the partridge family
to flinch or shrink back in fear

explanation.surface: A bird is said to be timid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small game bird and also means to shrink back in fear.

clue.text: Mark second vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Noting a second vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting mark left on the skin by a wound.

clue.text: Large house in ruin-no entry

indicators.note: entry shows one word going in to another

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country house lies in ruins, closed to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No entry' looks like a sign; read it as NO entering MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country house with its estate.

clue.text: Take cocaine, and a swift drink

definitions.meaning: to sniff a drug up the nose
a quick shot of spirits, a nip

explanation.surface: Two habits: cocaine and a quick tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is inhaling a drug through the nose; the noun is a quick tot of liquor.

clue.text: Workers' organisation look over unknown part of Italy

parts.note: TU is short for trade union
to scan is to look over
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A trade union inspects some mystery region of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is a region of central Italy, home to Florence.

clue.text: Non-proprietary info given to man

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: Information handed to a man is unbranded.
explanation.definitionFit: A generic product is sold without a brand or trademark name.

clue.text: Dismiss assembly

definitions.meaning: to expel or throw someone out
the number of people who come to an event

explanation.surface: Sending people away from a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to evict; as a noun it is the crowd attending.

clue.text: Walker rose

definitions.meaning: one who hikes in the countryside
a climbing variety of the flower

explanation.surface: A hiker who stood up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like a verb but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a hiker and also a climbing rose.

clue.text: Decline to describe Manx cat briefly?

definitions.meaning: to dwindle or fade away
the Manx cat is a breed born without a tail, so it is literally missing its rear appendage

explanation.surface: A brief description of a tailless Manx cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx cat, from the Isle of Man, is a breed with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to diminish gradually; literally a tail is absent.

clue.text: Contemptible person, to hire out present

parts.note: a cur is a worthless person or mongrel
to rent is to hire out

explanation.surface: A scoundrel lets out something now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' is the adjective meaning of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means belonging to the present time, contemporary.

clue.text: Dislike a copper coming round vineyard

indicators.note: coming round shows one piece surrounding the others

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to hate is to dislike

explanation.surface: Someone hates a policeman who visits a wine estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical symbol, split round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A French wine estate is named after its main building, so the word stands for a vineyard.

clue.text: Look hurt, perhaps, if one has this?

definitions.text: Look hurt, perhaps, if one has this?

parts.words: Look hurt, perhaps, if one has this?
parts.note: read look as a noun: a glance that harms, cast by someone with a malicious stare

explanation.walkthrough: 'Look hurt' reads as appearing upset, but means a glance that hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: Superstition holds that a malevolent stare can cause harm.

clue.text: Give me back my prize statuette

indicators.note: back signals that the word me is written in reverse

explanation.surface: Asking for one's trophy to be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give me back my prize' reads as a demand for a returned trophy; the 'back' belongs only to the word 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the statuette awarded for television achievement in America.

clue.text: Opera singer's new bed

parts.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer

explanation.surface: A soprano acquires a fresh bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a low bed or couch without a back.

clue.text: Weakness of deputy

definitions.meaning: a moral failing or bad habit
a stand-in, as in ...-president

explanation.surface: A failing in a second-in-command.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a moral failing and the prefix for a deputy.

clue.text: Chieftain Semiramis captured

indicators.note: captured means held within, so the answer is inside the name

explanation.surface: The legendary queen Semiramis took a chief prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: Semiramis was a legendary Assyrian queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or commander.

clue.text: Eagerly expecting silver to go up

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word go is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Anticipating silver prices rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means full of eager anticipation.

clue.text: Popular dance becomes forgotten

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the limbo is a Caribbean dance under a bar

explanation.surface: A once-fashionable dance has fallen out of memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left in suspension is neglected and overlooked.

clue.text: Painter was all Greek to the Spanish

definitions.text: Painter was all Greek to the Spanish

parts.words: Painter was all Greek to the Spanish
parts.note: the Cretan-born artist who worked in Toledo was known by the Spanish words for 'the Greek'

explanation.walkthrough: 'All Greek' suggests incomprehensible, but the painter's nickname literally means 'the Greek'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan-born painter Domenikos Theotokopoulos worked in Spain under this nickname.

clue.text: Court's wrong view of what may have caused accident?

definitions.meaning: a mistaken verdict by a court of law
a misjudgement behind a mishap, such as a driver's poor decision

explanation.surface: A court mistakenly blames the cause of a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a mistaken decision, legal or in everyday action.
